name: Value Stream Mapping
use_case: A flow diagram of every step a unit of work passes through from request to delivery, annotated with processing time and waiting time at each step, so the ratio of value-adding work to queueing becomes visible. Best used when lead time is the complaint — tickets, orders or features take weeks although the hands-on work is hours — and the team needs to see where the item is actually sitting idle rather than guessing which step is slow.
strengths: exposes waiting time, which is usually the dominant share of lead time
measures the end-to-end flow instead of optimising one team's local step
the current-state map is evidence, not opinion, about where delay lives
hand-off points between teams become impossible to ignore
weaknesses: mapping the current state accurately takes real observation, not a workshop
the map ages as soon as the process changes
manufacturing notation needs adapting for knowledge work
shows where delay occurs but not why, so pair it with a cause analysis
use_cases: A government permitting office takes months to approve applications that need only a few hours of review, and wants to see at which desk or department each file sits waiting before it redesigns the procedure.
A college admissions or student advising office wants to find where applications and student requests stall between offices, because students wait weeks for an answer that takes minutes to give.
A software organisation wants to see why a code change takes days to reach production, mapping each stage from commit through review, testing and release together with the waiting between them.
A hospital or clinic wants to understand why patients spend most of a visit or referral waiting, by following the patient journey step by step and timing each wait.
